Non-programmable calculators are allowed. Each question has FOUR suggested answers: A, B, C and D. Decide which answer is appropriate, find the number of the question on the answer sheet and draw a horizontal line across the letter to join the square brackets for the answer you have chosen. Mark only one answer for each question (if you mark more than one answer, you will score a zero for that question). Use a soft HB pencil.

questions.enonce_markdown: In the evolution of electronic computers, transistors were used in
questions.corrige_markdown: The generations of computers are defined by their main electronic component. First generation: vacuum tubes. **Second generation: transistors** (late 1950s to mid 1960s). Third generation: integrated circuits (ICs). Fourth generation: microprocessors (VLSI). The classic trap is to answer 'first' because transistors seem the oldest component, but the vacuum tube came before them. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which one of the following represents a picture file?
questions.corrige_markdown: The extension after the dot tells the type of file. **.jpg** (JPEG) is a compressed image format. .avi is a video file, .doc is a word-processed document and .ppt is a presentation. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In a word processor application, the program that provides synonyms of words is
questions.corrige_markdown: A **thesaurus** gives words with the same (or opposite) meaning, i.e. synonyms. A dictionary (spell checker) gives meanings and checks spelling, a translator converts text from one language to another, and an encyclopedia is a reference work on many subjects. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The security measure in a computer system that requires the use of network IP address is
questions.corrige_markdown: A **firewall** filters the traffic entering and leaving a network by examining packets, using rules based on IP addresses (and port numbers). A password checks the identity of a user, while encryption and decryption scramble and unscramble data; none of them depends on the IP address. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Software used only to create and edit text
questions.corrige_markdown: A (text) **editor** is used to type, create and modify plain text, for example the source code of a program. A compiler, an interpreter and an assembler are translators: they convert a program into machine code or run it, they do not create text. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The type of error in a program caused by the omission of a keyword in the programming language is called
questions.corrige_markdown: A **syntax error** breaks the grammar rules of the language: a missing keyword (for example a missing `THEN` or `END`), a missing bracket or a misspelt command. The translator detects it and refuses to run the program. Logic errors give wrong results although the program runs, and runtime errors occur while the program is executing (for example division by zero). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The implementation method in which an old system is totally replaced by a new one at once
questions.corrige_markdown: In **plunge** (direct) changeover the old system is switched off and the new one takes over immediately. Phased changeover introduces the new system part by part, pilot changeover tests it in one branch or department first, and parallel changeover runs both systems side by side for some time. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The computer RAM cannot be replaced by ROM because
questions.corrige_markdown: RAM is the working memory: programs and data are constantly written to it and changed while the computer runs. **The data in ROM is fixed** (read-only, written by the manufacturer), so ROM cannot hold changing data. 'Non-volatile' is true of ROM but it is an advantage, not a reason why ROM cannot replace RAM. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The organization of files on a disk constitute a
questions.corrige_markdown: Of the four options, only a **database** is an organised collection of files (tables) of related data stored on a disk. A field is a single item of data, a record is a group of related fields, and a query is a request made to a database. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The conversion of digital signals to analogue signals is an example of
questions.corrige_markdown: **Modulation** converts the digital signal of the computer into an analogue signal that can travel on a telephone line (this is what a modem does at the sending end). The reverse operation, analogue to digital, is demodulation. 'Moderation' and 'demoderation' are not computing terms. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The network device used to determine the best path for a data packet across networks is called
questions.corrige_markdown: A **router** reads the destination address of each packet and chooses the best route to forward it between networks. A repeater only regenerates a weak signal, a bridge joins two segments of the same network, and a linker is a program utility, not a network device. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The point on the command line interface where instructions are entered is called
questions.corrige_markdown: In a command line interface the **prompt** (for example `C:>`) shows that the system is ready and is where the user types a command. The cursor is the blinking mark that shows the typing position; 'space' and 'entry' are not standard terms. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A program that detects errors in a program code is called
questions.corrige_markdown: A **debugger** is the tool designed to find (detect) errors in program code, for example by running it step by step and watching the variables. A compiler mainly translates the program (it only reports syntax errors on the way), an assembler translates assembly language, and a decoder interprets instructions or codes. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The CPU system bus consists of
questions.corrige_markdown: The system bus has three parts: the **data bus** (carries data), the **address bus** (carries the location in memory) and the **control bus** (carries control signals such as read or write). There is no 'memory bus' in this list of three. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An example of spreadsheet mixed cell reference is
questions.corrige_markdown: A mixed reference fixes only one part of the address. **A\$2** keeps the row fixed (2) while the column can change when the formula is copied. \$A\$2 is an absolute reference (both parts fixed), and \$2\$A and 2\$A are not valid cell addresses because the column letter must come before the row number. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The protocol that governs the downloading of files on the Internet is
questions.corrige_markdown: **FTP** (File Transfer Protocol) is used to upload and download files between computers. HTTP transfers web pages, IP addresses and routes packets, and ISP (Internet Service Provider) is a company, not a protocol. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In SDLC, preliminary investigation is done during
questions.corrige_markdown: In the System Development Life Cycle the first stage is the preliminary investigation, which is the **feasibility study**: it decides whether the project is technically, economically and operationally possible. Analysis and design come afterwards. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The computation of the logic operation on the strings of bits (10010) AND (01011) gives
questions.corrige_markdown:
AND gives 1 only when both bits are 1. Bit by bit:

| | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AND | 0 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 1 |
| = | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 |

The result is **00010** (checked by script). The trap is to use OR, which would give 11011. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Two components of a data transmission system include
questions.corrige_markdown: Every data transmission system needs at least a **sender** (source), a **receiver** (destination) and a transmission medium. Of the options, only 'sender and receiver' are two components of the system itself. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The result of computing $1101_2 + 101_2$ is
questions.corrige_markdown:
Convert to denary: $1101_2 = 13$ and $101_2 = 5$, so the sum is $13 + 5 = 18$. Now $18 = 16 + 2 = 10010_2$. Directly in binary:

```
  1101
+  101
------
 10010
```

The result is **$10010_2$** (checked by script). **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The acronym PIN code stands for
questions.corrige_markdown: PIN stands for **Personal Identification Number**: a secret number that identifies the holder of a card or account. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Program written in HTML is interpreted by
questions.corrige_markdown: HTML is a markup language: a web **browser** reads the tags and displays the page. The Internet is only the network that carries the page. HTML is not compiled, and the translation is done by the browser, not by a general programming-language interpreter. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The exact number of floppy discs each of size 4MB needed to hold 2GB of data is
questions.corrige_markdown: Computer storage uses powers of 2: $1\text{ GB} = 1024\text{ MB}$, so $2\text{ GB} = 2048\text{ MB}$. Number of discs $= 2048 \div 4 = 512$ (checked by script). The answer 500 comes from wrongly using $1\text{ GB} = 1000\text{ MB}$, but the question asks for the *exact* number. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: When data is being transferred from a fast storage to a slower storage, the computer processor regulates the data flow rate by making use of
questions.corrige_markdown: A **buffer** is a small area of memory that temporarily holds data while it moves between devices working at different speeds, so the fast device does not overrun the slow one. A controller manages a device, RAM chips are the main memory in general, and virtual memory extends RAM using the disk. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The pair of html tags that generates a numbered list is
questions.corrige_markdown:
`
    ` ... `
` is an **ordered list**, shown with numbers. `
    ` is an unordered (bulleted) list, `` makes text bold, and `
  • ` marks each item inside either kind of list. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Signals into and out of a company's extranet is protected from outside intruders using
questions.corrige_markdown: A **firewall** controls the traffic entering and leaving a network and blocks unauthorised access from outside. Encryption protects the content of data, not the entry point, and cameras and solid structures protect the building, not the network signals. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: How many symbols are there in the hexadecimal number system?
questions.corrige_markdown: Hexadecimal is base 16, so it has **16 symbols**: 0 to 9 and A to F (A=10, B=11, C=12, D=13, E=14, F=15). Answer 15 is the largest value of one digit, not the number of symbols. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The smallest data storage unit on a magnetic disk is
questions.corrige_markdown: A magnetic disk is divided into concentric tracks, and each track is cut into **sectors**, the smallest unit that can be read or written (traditionally 512 bytes). A cluster is a group of sectors, and a cylinder is the set of tracks at the same position on all platters. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the hardware secures the computer from the effect of power spikes, and voltage fluctuations?
questions.corrige_markdown: An **Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS)** contains a battery and a regulator: it smooths spikes and voltage fluctuations and keeps the computer running during a power cut. 'Interruptible power supply' is not a real device. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following describes a transmission mode between a computer and a printer during the printing?
questions.corrige_markdown: During printing, data flows in **one direction only**, from the computer to the printer: this is simplex transmission (like a television broadcast). Half duplex allows both directions but one at a time, and full duplex (duplex) allows both directions at once. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The term video conferencing means
questions.corrige_markdown: Video conferencing lets people in different places meet in real time using cameras, microphones, screens and a network link: **a remote meeting with participants at distant locations**. The other options describe local presentations in one place. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Running a conference using video projectors
Holding a remote meeting using multimedia tools and links with participants at distant locations.
Use of large television screens to manage an outdoor conference
Use of video and audio facilities to run a conference in a large hall

questions.enonce_markdown: The Data check that requires users to enter their secret codes two times before granting access is called
questions.corrige_markdown: **Verification** checks that data was entered correctly, typically by entering it twice and comparing the two entries (as when you choose a new password). Validation checks that data is reasonable (range check, type check), and a parity check detects errors in transmitted bits. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A graphical representation of a software tool or action is called a(an)
questions.corrige_markdown: An **icon** is a small picture that represents a program, a file, a tool or an action in a graphical user interface. A folder is a container for files, and a file is a named set of data. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The octal (base 8) equivalent of the binary number $10011011_2$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: Group the bits in threes starting from the right: $10\,011\,011$, i.e. $010\,011\,011$. Each group is an octal digit: $010 = 2$, $011 = 3$, $011 = 3$. So the number is **$233_8$** (checked by script: $10011011_2 = 155_{10} = 233_8$). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Laptop computers are examples of
questions.corrige_markdown: Laptops, desktops and tablets are **microcomputers**: small computers built around a microprocessor and meant for one user. Supercomputers, mainframes and minicomputers are much larger machines shared by many users. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A barcode reader is an example of a(an)
questions.corrige_markdown: A barcode reader scans the bars and sends the code into the computer: it is an **input device**. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The full meaning of QR code is
questions.corrige_markdown: QR stands for **Quick Response**: the two-dimensional code was designed to be read quickly by a scanner or a phone camera. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The stage from which data is stored on hard disks is
questions.corrige_markdown: The stages of the information processing cycle are input, processing, output and storage. Data is saved on hard disks and other media at the **storage stage**. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Software designed to store, retrieve, manipulate and update data is
questions.corrige_markdown: **Database management software** (DBMS) is designed to store data in an organised way and to retrieve, manipulate and update it. A spreadsheet calculates, a word processor handles text and accounting software handles financial records. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The category of software that enables the computer to manage its internal resources is called
questions.corrige_markdown: **System software** (the operating system, utilities and drivers) manages the processor, memory, storage and devices. Application software does tasks for the user, and custom software is written for one customer. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In database normalization, composite attributes are converted to atomic (individual) attribute in order to
questions.corrige_markdown: Splitting a composite attribute (for example a full address) into atomic attributes is the first step of normalisation (first normal form). The purpose of normalisation is to **eliminate data anomalies** (insertion, update and deletion anomalies) and to reduce redundancy, not to increase it. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Eliminate various forms of data anomalies

questions.enonce_markdown: The maximum signal carrying capacity of a communication channel is referred to as
questions.corrige_markdown: **Bandwidth** is the maximum amount of data (or range of frequencies) a channel can carry. Hertz is only the unit of frequency, and broadband is a type of fast connection. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: One disadvantage of computer simulations is that
questions.corrige_markdown: A simulation is only a model: if the model or its data are wrong or simplified, the results **may give a wrong impression of the real situation**. The other options are not real drawbacks; simulations are cheap, safe and often lead to discoveries. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: It may give wrong impression of the real situation
It leads to suspension of work in the company

questions.enonce_markdown: The installation of Windows 10 in replacement of Windows 8 in a computer is an example of Software
questions.corrige_markdown: Moving to a newer major version of the same software is an **upgrade**. An update only applies small fixes or patches to the version you already have. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The full meaning of the abbreviation SSD storage in computers is
questions.corrige_markdown: SSD stands for **Solid State Device** (more often written Solid State Drive): storage built from flash memory chips with no moving parts. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The type of processor used in laundry machines is
questions.corrige_markdown: A washing machine contains a small processor built into the machine to do one dedicated job: an **embedded processor** (embedded system). A general-purpose microprocessor is used in computers, and 'simple' and 'domestic' processors are not standard terms. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A multiplexer receives signals from
questions.corrige_markdown: A multiplexer (MUX) selects one of **many inputs** and sends it through **one output**. The opposite device, one input to several outputs, is a demultiplexer. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: One input and emits through several outputs
Many inputs and emits through one output
Many inputs and emits through many outputs
One input and emits through one output

questions.enonce_markdown: Program code that is neither compiled nor interpreted is
questions.corrige_markdown: **Source code** is the program as written by the programmer in a high-level language. As long as it has not been passed to a compiler or an interpreter it is neither compiled nor interpreted. Object code is the result of compilation, and 'program code' and 'raw code' are not standard terms. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The term softcopy in computing refers to
questions.corrige_markdown: A **softcopy** is output that exists in electronic form, for example on the screen or in a file. Printed copies are hardcopy. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Who is responsible for the coordination of the Development of an information system
questions.corrige_markdown: The **project manager** plans, organises and coordinates the people, time and resources of the development of an information system. The system analyst studies the needs and designs the solution, and the programmer writes the code. **Answer: D.**
